page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c4g1.xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine designed for entry-level machine learning inference and graphic workloads. Powered by the KVM hypervisor on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The CPU subsystem is supported by 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512, and AES. System memory totals 15.0 GB (3.75 GB per vCPU), and network throughput is rated at a 4 Gbps baseline. The instance carries no local storage, requiring network-attached cloud storage for disk persistence.

Hardware acceleration is delivered by a dedicated NVIDIA Turing T4 GPU equipped with 16 GB of VRAM. Benchmark results emphasize the division between host compute and GPU capability. General CPU execution and memory subsystem speeds land in the lower quartiles, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 933.0, a multi-core score of 2077.0, and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 20.81 GB/sec. Similarly, general data processing tasks such as bzip3 decompression and static web serving register in the bottom 25% of tested servers.

In contrast, the integrated NVIDIA T4 accelerator delivers competitive performance for deep learning inference. LLM benchmarks report prompt processing speeds of 8480.06 tokens per second on a small 135M model and 1167.65 tokens per second on a 7B model, placing prompt ingestion in the top 10% tier. Text generation achieves 263.82 tokens per second for the 135M model and 34.5 tokens per second for the 7B model. Larger parameter footprints like 70B models cannot be served due to the 16 GB VRAM ceiling.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, ecs.gn6i-c4g1.xlarge provides an economical entry point for GPU acceleration by pairing a modern-enough accelerator with an older generation host CPU. The primary architectural tradeoff is limited host compute and modest memory throughput, making this server best suited for lightweight AI inference serving, computer vision processing, and GPU-driven rendering rather than host-intensive data preparation or high-concurrency database workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c4g1.xlarge is an entry-tier GPU-accelerated server instance built for targeted machine learning and graphics workflows. Running on KVM and x86_64 architecture, it combines 4 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8163 processor at 2.5 GHz with 15.0 GB of system memory and a 4 Gbps baseline network link. Accelerated compute is handled by a single NVIDIA T4 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM, with zero bundled local storage. Synthetic benchmarks show modest host CPU performance, reflected in lower-tier Geekbench and memory bandwidth results. However, the NVIDIA T4 yields high-efficiency prompt processing and text generation speeds for small to mid-sized language models up to 7B parameters. The hardware profile makes this instance well matched for cost-effective AI model serving, computer vision inference, and lightweight GPU processing.
